title: Two Sum
description: Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to target. You may assume each input has exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice. Return the answer in any order.
hints: Think about what information would make finding the second number instant.
If you store each number you've seen along with its index, you can check the complement (target - current) in O(1).
solution_approach: Iterate once, inserting each value into a hash map keyed by value → index. For each element, check whether target - num is already in the map; if so return both indices.
common_mistakes: Returning the same element twice by checking the map before inserting the current element.
Using a nested loop which gives O(N^2) time.
similar_problems: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted

brute_force.description: Check every pair of indices. For each i, look for target - nums[i] in the rest of the array.

better.description: One pass storing each number and its index in a hash map. For each element, check if the complement target - num is already in the map.

optimal.description: The single-pass hash map approach above is already optimal (O(N) time). The two-pointer technique also works but requires the array to be sorted, so the hash map is preferred for the classic unsorted version.
